b.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's ICP as rules, scored by hand for restaurants in Ibadan (names below are the lab's invented ones).

RulePointsSource
Google rating 4.0 or higher25Google Maps listing
100 or more reviews15Google Maps listing
Offers delivery25Business's own website
Offers office lunches20Business's own website
Address in Bodija, Mokola, Ring Road, Akobo or Dugbe15Google Maps listing
Disqualify: not a restaurant, or outside the zoneoutGoogle Maps category and address
No published business emailmanual listBusiness's own website

Keep anyone scoring 60 or more. Sample of the 20:

BusinessScoreNext step
Amala Corner (4.6, 812, delivery, office lunch, Bodija)100Email
Iya Basira Kitchen (4.3, 240, delivery, Mokola, no published email)80Manual: call off-peak
The Grill Yard (4.7, 1,320, no delivery, Ring Road)55Park
Mama Put Express (3.8, 95, delivery, Dugbe)40Park
Sweet Crumbs BakeryoutBakery, outside ICP

Test: give the rules to a friend with five of your businesses. Same scores means the rules are clear.
mistakes: Writing feelings as rules ('busy', 'serious') that no source can check.
Leaving out where each rule's answer comes from.
Using LinkedIn scraping, a browser extension or a bought list to find the 20.
Treating 'no business email' as a low score instead of a separate manual route.
b.pass: Every rule has points and a named allowed source, 20 businesses are scored, and a second person scoring five of them from the rules gets the same numbers.
b.redo: Send it back if any rule cannot be checked from a named source, any lead came from a banned source, or a second scorer gets different results.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's agent on 10 real Ibadan restaurants, every send going to your own test inbox.

  1. HTTP Request · Places Text Search, field mask places.id,places.displayName,places.rating,places.userRatingCount,places.websiteUri,places.formattedAddress; key in a Header Auth credential. Store only place_id.
  2. HTTP Request (home and menu pages, 2-second wait) → HTML (extract text) → Information Extractor with offers_delivery, office_lunch, business_email, fact, fact_quote.
  3. Code · verify: keep fact only if fact_quote (over 12 characters) appears in the page text.
  4. Code · score, then keep 60 or more:
    let s = 0;
if ($json.rating >= 4.0) s += 25;
if ($json.userRatingCount >= 100) s += 15;
if ($json.offers_delivery) s += 25;
if ($json.office_lunch) s += 20;
const zone = /bodija|mokola|ring road|akobo|dugbe/i.test($json.formattedAddress);
if (zone) s += 15;
const route = !zone ? 'out' : $json.business_email ? 'email' : 'manual';
return { ...$json, fit_score: s, route };
  5. AI drafts from the template, filling only {{business}} and {{fact}}; no verified fact means a general line about kitchens in the area.
  6. Code · lint: 120 words or fewer, exactly one question, no spam words or shouting, honest subject. It appends "Tolu Adebayo, Harvest Lane, Bodija, Ibadan. Not useful? Reply STOP and I won't email again."
  7. Telegram · Send and Wait: name, score, reasons, fact with source link, draft; Approve, Edit, Skip.
  8. Gmail · Send with To fixed to your test address, never business_email.

Log: 10 found, 7 scored 60+, 6 verified facts, 1 general line, 7 lint passes, 6 approved, 0 sent to businesses.
mistakes: Using * as the Places field mask, or storing copies of Places data instead of the place ID.
Asking the AI to 'be honest' instead of checking the quote against the page text in code.
Letting the AI write the opt-out and identity, so some drafts miss them.
Wiring the Gmail To field to business_email while testing.
Scoring with the AI instead of a Code node.
s.pass: Executions for 10 real businesses show the verify node, a code-calculated score, lint passes for every draft, Telegram approvals, and sends that reached only the learner's test inbox.
s.redo: Send it back if any fact is unverified, a draft fails the lint, the field mask is *, Places data is stored, or any email reached a real business.

g.answer:
Worked example: Kemi Packaging, a fictional food-packaging wholesaler in Ibadan, prospecting restaurants and hotels for two weeks. The client signed off the ICP, the template and the rules before day 1.

Setup: outreach subdomain, 20 a day maximum, the owner approves every draft on Telegram, suppression checked before every send, one follow-up after 5 working days.

MeasureWeek 1Week 2Total
Prospects found (allowed sources)8461145
Fit 60+ with business email382765
Manual list (form or phone)171229
Drafts approved302454
Sent (incl. follow-ups)304171
Replies: interested347
Replies: not now235
Replies: STOP123
Out of office / bounce / other235
Meetings booked134
Complaints000

All three STOPs and two bounces were on the suppression list within the hour; none received a follow-up. No facts were sent unverified.

What we learned: verified facts about a new menu or branch got the most replies; general lines got almost none. Hotels replied within a day, restaurants took about four.

Client decision: continue for four more weeks, hotels and caterers only, because restaurant replies were slower.

Submit: the signed-off ICP and template, the Prospects and Suppression sheets (business data only), this report, and the client's written decision.
mistakes: Starting before the client has approved the ICP, template and rules in writing.
Sending from the client's main domain or above the daily cap.
Reporting only emails sent, with no breakdown of replies by type or meetings.
Leaving a STOP reply in the follow-up queue.
g.pass: A two-week report with prospects found, approved, sent, replies by type, meetings and opt-outs; evidence that every opt-out was suppressed within a day; zero complaints; and the client's written decision.
g.redo: Send it back if there was any complaint, an opt-out was followed up, the cap or subdomain rule was broken, or the client's decision is missing.
